h: The Midrash: the soul that sees and guards

p: "Bless the LORD, O my soul," etc.
that he blessed the Holy One, blessed be He, with the soul?
Because the soul sees and is not seen, etc.;
the soul guards the body, etc.
it counts five "Bless, O my soul"
as said corresponding to the soul,
the five levels within the soul

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10a — הָנֵי חֲמִשָּׁה "בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי" כְּנֶגֶד מִי אֲמָרָן דָּוִד? לֹא אֲמָרָן אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּכְנֶגֶד נְשָׁמָה: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא כָּל הָעוֹלָם — אַף נְשָׁמָה מְלֵאָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף; … רוֹאֶה וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה …; … זָן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ — אַף נְשָׁמָה זָנָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף; … טָהוֹר — אַף נְשָׁמָה טְהוֹרָה; … יוֹשֵׁב בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים — אַף נְשָׁמָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים ("Fills … sees and is not seen … nourishes … is pure … dwells in the innermost chambers"). Rav Tzadok reads the five clauses in order as the stages of a person's life: from conception (fills and guards), to first sight in Torah, to thirteen (nourishes), to purity, to the innermost chambers (zaken). Editorial corrections made from this Gemara: the printing's "שהנשמה זכה את (כל) הגוף" (twice) is corrected to זנה (the Gemara's "nourishes", which is the third clause and the one his explanation needs); "ואינה נראה" → נראית; "יוש" → יושב.

h: Filling and guarding the body from conception

p: "so too the neshamah fills the whole body,"
Just as it lists regarding God, blessed be He,
that He fills the whole world,
"and the Holy One, blessed be He, guards the entire world"
from when the body is formed,
even though it has no understanding at all
for the soul is given to a person
and it guards the whole body.

rich.text: — נְשָׁמָה מֵאֵימָתַי נִיתְּנָה בָּאָדָם, מִשְּׁעַת פְּקִידָה אוֹ מִשְּׁעַת יְצִירָה? … אֶלָּא מִשְּׁעַת פְּקִידָה ("From when is the soul given to a person, from conception or from formation? … From conception"), Antoninus and Rabbi. p: when he merits to grasp something of the words of Torah,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
along the lines of what was explained elsewhere
"A maidservant saw at the Sea…" etc.
And this is what it says:
"so too the neshamah sees and is not seen."
merits sight in words of Torah,
that the body too should grasp
something of the words of Torah;
that is, that he come to hold
the words of Torah as a possession,
so that it is fixed in the body as well.

h: Thirteen: the soul nourishes the body

p: when he becomes thirteen years old
that the soul *nourishes* the whole body,
so that he draws life from the words of Torah,
"May He open our heart to His Torah."

rich.text: — הוּא יִפְתַּח לִבֵּנוּ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ ("May He open our heart to His Torah"). This is the stage where Torah enters the heart and gives "life." The printing's "לבינו" is corrected to לבנו.

h: Purity: the evil inclination returns, and is slaughtered only in the future

p: just as at the time of the Giving of the Torah
for the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts,
the evil inclination returned to its place,
so too, even after he merits
that the soul nourishes the body,
so that he draws life from words of Torah,
for the power of the evil inclination is nullified.
the evil inclination has not been cleared away
